dct_description_sm: Development of a killer whale sightings database was started in 2005. Killer whales are poorly known in Arctic Canada, and Inuit have been reporting increased presence. Opportunistic sightings have been compiled from a variety of sources, including peer-reviewed journal articles, government reports, consulting documents, newspapers, and personal communications with northern residents and researchers. Extensive efforts to collect Inuit knowledge included 105 semi-directed interviews conducted in 11 Nunavut communities. The most recent update of the database (Higdon et al., in press) includes > 400 records with associated information on group size, predation, seasonal distirbution, behaviour, etc.
dct_title_s: Killer whale (Orcinus orca) sightings in the Canadian Arctic
